title: Stabilizing and detecting electron fractionalization in the Hofstadter-Hubbard model
authors: Jiahao Yang, Zeyu Han, Gang v. Chen
abstract: Motivated by the recent progress in correlated Chern insulator physics in moiré systems, we investigate the half-filled triangular-lattice Hofstadter--Hubbard model and its electron fractionalization. Among various competing non-magnetic states, increasing the orbital flux stabilizes and broadens the $\mathrm{U}(1)_2$ chiral spin liquid phase in the Mott regime. In this exotic regime, the electron is fractionalized into gapped spinons and gapped chargons, whose effective bands are linked to the orbital flux. The convolution of the narrow spinon bands with the gapped chargon excitations produces rich and discernible structures in the electron spectral function and the density of states. These results not only identify the orbital flux as a control parameter for the detailed patterns of electron fractionalization and the nature of the Mott transition, but also provide the key spectral characteristics for the angle-resolved photoemission and scanning tunneling studies of the relevant systems, linking the free-particle band topology to intrinsic topological order in the correlated regime.
summary: This theoretical study analyzes electron fractionalization in the Hofstadter-Hubbard model on a triangular lattice under an external magnetic flux. Using a slave-rotor mean-field approach, the authors show that the magnetic flux stabilizes a U(1)2 chiral spin liquid (CSL) phase. The key diagnostic tool is the electron spectral function, which reveals distinct convolution patterns in the CSL compared to other correlated phases.
main_problem: The paper investigates how noninteracting band topologies evolve under strong correlations, specifically focusing on electron fractionalization in the Mott insulating regime.
main_result: Increasing the orbital magnetic flux stabilizes and broadens the U(1)2 chiral spin liquid (CSL) phase, which is characterized by distinct spectral signatures derived from the convolution of spinon and chargon excitations.
method: The study employs a self-consistent slave-rotor mean-field theory to decompose the electron operator into fractionalized spinon and rotor components.
model_or_system: The system is the half-filled triangular-lattice Hofstadter-Hubbard model, analyzed in the presence of an external magnetic flux ($\Phi_{ext}$). The Hamiltonian is studied across various competing non-magnetic states like Chern Insulator (CI), CSL, and Valence-Bond Solid (VBS).
key_observables: Electron spectral function $A_e(k, \omega)$, local density of states $ho_e(\omega)$, topological invariants (Chern number), and condensate weight ($Z$).
important_parameters: Orbital flux ($\Phi_{ext}^{	riangle}$), interaction strength ($U/t$), and filling factor (half-filled case).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on slave-rotor mean-field theory and neglects residual vertex corrections when calculating the electron propagator.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate mean-field phase diagrams mapping out CI, CSL, and VBS regions as a function of flux and interaction strength. Spectral functions show characteristic multi-peak structures in the CSL, contrasting with the coherent contribution in the CI.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the model and the fractionalization ansatz, then calculating ground-state energies and phase diagrams comparing CI, CSL, and VBS. Finally, it analyzes the spectral properties by calculating the electron Green function as a convolution of spinon and rotor propagators to distinguish the phases.
why_interesting: The explicit link between topological band structure (Chern insulators) and intrinsic topological order in the correlated regime, mediated by fractionalization, is highly relevant to understanding exotic quantum states in strongly correlated materials.
